description: Executable Candidate recipe of NVIDIA's DGX Spark playbook (vllm) for Llama 3.1 405B Instruct AWQ INT4: vllm 0.21.0+2325b6f0 (NVIDIA NGC vllm 26.05.post1-py3), pinned by arm64 digest, serving the exact model revision through `vllm serve` with the playbook's flags (vLLM defaults where the playbook passes none). Tensor parallel 4 across four Sparks uses vLLM's native multi-node launch (the platform's --nnodes/--node-rank placement options) instead of the playbook's hand-started Ray cluster: the pinned NVIDIA NGC vllm 26.05.post1 image does not ship Ray (its layers hold no ray package and no ray executable), and vLLM rejects --nnodes with the Ray executor. Deviation from the playbook: the context is 512 tokens (batched tokens 512) instead of 64, so the sweep's 256-token A323 chat case plus its prompt fits the context and the bounded 64-token chat check fits too. Four Sparks, not two: the AWQ INT4 checkpoint is 204.22 GiB, so a pair holds 109.64 GB of weights per rank, and loading needs at least 16 GB more on top. Hardware-observed on two Sparks (tensor parallel 2): on 2026-11-01 (utilization 0.85) both ranks died during weight loading (the host guard stopped one worker at MemAvailable 0 and the kernel OOM-killed the other), and in the 2026-11-03 sweep at the creator's gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 both ranks were OOM-killed at start; swap stayed unused because the weights land in GPU/driver memory. NVIDIA's own playbook notes insufficient memory headroom on two Sparks (README line 434) and marks that setup testing only. At tensor parallel 4 (128 attention heads and 16 KV heads divide evenly) each rank holds about 54.8 GB of weights. Memory follows the creator's settings: GPU memory utilization 0.9 with no explicit KV pool, the playbook's 405B launch at 98b3a473 (nvidia/vllm/README.md line 451). The declared peak is the admission maximum, an estimate until a four-rank run measures it; physical acceptance is pending. It needs four enrolled Sparks.
title: Llama 3.1 405B Instruct AWQ INT4 vLLM four Sparks (NVIDIA playbook)
